title: P1 death-return response
description: Response of POST /p1/actor/death-return (DEC-DEATH-RETURN-20261105). On a committed return, result carries the server-owned anchor the actor was moved to, the HP the approved formula produced, the counts of combat state actually cleared and the tick the next return is allowed from. A replay of a key that already committed answers 200 with the same recorded snapshot and applied=false/replayed=true, and never moves, heals or restarts a cooldown a second time; requests rejected before the session resolves omit sessionId and result. Every coordinate here is an output and never an input.

applied.description: true only on the commit. A replay of a key that already committed is false, with replayed true.

xWu.description: The approved safe anchor the actor was placed on, clamped into that map's bounds. Not a client input.

hp.description: max(1, ceil(currentEffectiveMaxHp * 0.5)) on a commit; on a replay this is the HP the original commit produced, which is why a client must fresh-read the world after a receipt.

mp.description: Kept at its current absolute value and clamped to maxMp. No source restores MP on a return.

serverTick.description: Server clock tick of the commit. At 20 Hz one tick is 0,05 s.

revision.description: The session aggregate revision the return advanced by exactly one, and the value a replay repeats.

inflightCasts.description: Casts cancelled by this return, counted from the CANCEL/END pairs the engine emitted.

reservedCounters.description: Counters reserved for a later tick that this return cancelled.

guardWindowClosed.description: true only when a window was still open for this actor; a death that already closed it reports false.

movementWindowReset.description: design.clear 'movement held intent': /p1/move integrates an elapsed window, so clearing it means restarting that window on the server, which this return always does.

penalties.description: Echoed so a client never has to guess. The approved design sets all three to zero; a non-zero penalty requires a new decision, which this schema refuses.

nextReturnAllowedAtTick.description: successfulApplyTick + cooldownTicks (three seconds = 60 ticks at 20 Hz under DESIGN-BM-ALPHA-20261103). null only on the pre-alpha fixture shape, where no source defines a cooldown. A refusal or a replay never moves it.

Carried by death_return_cooldown so a client can schedule its retry from the server's tick instead of inferring how long a retryable refusal meant. Refusals that changed nothing leave the deadline of the return that set it.
